source_snapshot.procedure: In BMC WebUI Hardware status > Inventory and LEDs, check Fans information and detail information.
source_snapshot.criteria: Data readable/correct; every fan status fits actual status; fan speed correct.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES assumes `/Chassis/FRU_SYS/Thermal`, limits selection to range(0;8), then pipes the Fans array into an expression that attempts `.Fans[$i]` on that array. It cannot establish sixteen exact `_F` channel identities, physical mapping, units, thresholds or freshness.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly restores all sixteen mapped channels, unit-aware telemetry and no-control safety, but treats finite topology, suffix semantics and approved ranges as a continuing decision rather than bounded execution prerequisites.

old_problem: The suggested query covers at most half of the named channels, is structurally unreliable after the jq pipe, assumes an OEM chassis path, and provides no authoritative way to decide whether each speed/status is correct. The prior review found these defects but retained Pending for the Project fan map, `_F` meaning and operating ranges.
disposition_reason: Discover the target chassis and supported modern Fan collection or legacy Thermal representation, enumerate every page/member, bind SPD_FAN1_F through SPD_FAN16_F individually through the approved fan/rotor/controller map, and compare unit-aware speed, state, health, presence, thresholds and freshness to approved limits for the captured operating context and actual WebUI. The map, suffix definition and limits are required Project configuration, not unresolved engineering semantics.
decision_basis: XLSX row 970, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 971 were directly reviewed; next pending was verified as Functionality row 971 / variant e6ee840e716640bd.

DMTF defines a modern Fan collection below a discovered Chassis ThermalSubsystem and a Fan resource with Status, Location and SpeedPercent data; older services can expose fan readings in the legacy Thermal resource. The service-advertised schema and links, not a fixed `FRU_SYS` URI, determine the parser.
The testcase explicitly names sixteen `_F` channels. Each must be accounted exactly once; array order, substring matching, eight indices or aggregate healthy state cannot preserve that coverage.

Fan-speed correctness is contextual. The approved mapping must define `_F`, installed population, units and acceptable range/threshold for the relevant fan-control, redundancy, power and workload state. No numeric threshold is invented.

ED-08, ED-14, ED-15, ED-17, ED-19, ED-21 and ED-30 require actual WebUI evidence, formal thresholds, preserved logs and all sixteen independent identities; ED-33 through ED-38 permit safe parameterization and prohibit PWM/control, disconnect, injection, power/reset and automatic retry.

test_case.test_name: Validate SPD_FAN1_F through SPD_FAN16_F status and speed independently
test_case.purpose: Verify all sixteen exact `_F` fan speed/status channels are present as expected, mapped to the correct physical fan/rotor/controller input, fresh, healthy and within the approved unit-aware operating range for the captured system and fan-control context, and reconcile them with the actual BMC WebUI without changing cooling behavior.
required_package: Immutable SUT/BMC/chassis/firmware/WebUI identity and authoritative definition of `_F` plus SPD_FAN1_F..SPD_FAN16_F-to-physical fan/rotor/controller mapping

Approved expected sixteen-channel population and per-channel presence, state, health, reading unit, valid range/threshold and staleness policy for each supported power/load/redundancy/fan-control context
Service-root-discovered Chassis/ThermalSubsystem/Fan collection or documented legacy Thermal representation, pagination and member-to-channel binding
Schema-aware normalization for modern Fan SpeedPercent.Reading/SpeedRPM and Status/Location or legacy Thermal Fans Reading/ReadingUnits/thresholds
Read-only source for captured power, workload, redundancy and fan-control context; actual rendered WebUI Fans table/detail mapping
Trusted TLS/protected credentials, baseline/post SEL and audit acquisition without deletion, time synchronization, redaction and evidence storage
test_case.test_command: READ ONLY. Verify immutable target and capture power/load/redundancy/fan-control context. Discover the selected Chassis and its advertised ThermalSubsystem/Fans links; if the target exposes only the legacy Thermal resource, use its advertised schema. Traverse every collection page/member and preserve complete redacted raw records. Resolve exactly SPD_FAN1_F through SPD_FAN16_F with the approved suffix and physical fan/rotor/controller map; do not use member order, substring-only matching or `range(0;8)`. For each channel record durable ID, physical/service label, expected/observed presence, Status.State/Health, numeric speed value and declared unit, supported percent/RPM/control-context data, applicable lower/upper thresholds, acquisition time and freshness. Open and capture the actual rendered WebUI fan table and every required detail, then compare API/UI/reference values within approved sampling skew and tolerance. Preserve baseline and post-test SEL/audit evidence without clearing it. Do not set PWM or override mode, change thresholds, disconnect/reseat/stop a fan, inject a fault, apply workload, reboot/reset or power-cycle.
test_case.expected_result: Each of SPD_FAN1_F..SPD_FAN16_F appears exactly once and maps unambiguously to the approved physical channel. Expected population, state and health match actual read-only evidence; every speed is numeric, fresh, expressed in the expected unit and within the approved range/threshold for the recorded operating context. Actual WebUI and API/telemetry agree within approved tolerance, all sixteen identities remain distinct, logs contain no unexpected cooling fault, and fan controls and system state are unchanged.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires explicit 16-of-16 identity accounting, authoritative `_F`/physical mapping, complete collection traversal, unit-aware fresh speed comparison against approved contextual ranges, acceptable state/health/presence, actual rendered WebUI detail and preserved log reconciliation. Eight samples, aggregate fan health, name substring, RPM alone or a WebUI list without details cannot pass. A missing/extra/duplicate/ambiguous channel, wrong mapping/unit, stale/unparseable/out-of-range reading, unacceptable state/health, unexpected log or API/UI/reference mismatch is FAIL. Missing mapping, suffix meaning, operating context or approved range is NOT READY rather than Pending, and no threshold is invented.
safety_gate: Use only certificate-verified protected GET/read operations and service-advertised links/schema; do not assume `FRU_SYS`, collection order or a fixed modern/legacy shape.
Account for all sixteen exact names independently and bind them through the approved physical topology; `_F` meaning must not be guessed.
Capture power/load/redundancy/control context and units before threshold comparison; RPM, percent command and actual tachometer reading are not interchangeable.
Preserve baseline logs before any contemplated deletion; this read-only testcase never clears SEL, system logs or audit history.
Prohibit PWM/full-speed override or threshold changes, fan disconnect/reseat/stop, fault injection, workload stimulus, reboot/reset and all power transitions.
Stop on missing/duplicate mapping, stale data, cooling fault or source disagreement; preserve evidence and do not automatically retry or stimulate the fan.
expected_evidence: Immutable target/schema/WebUI identity, authoritative `_F` definition and complete sixteen-channel physical fan/rotor/controller map
Complete modern Fan collection or legacy Thermal raw artifacts with advertised links, pagination/member list, timestamps and hashes
Per-channel 16-row matrix containing identity/location, expected/observed presence, state/health, speed value/unit, contextual range/threshold, freshness and verdict
Captured power/load/redundancy/fan-control context and calculations showing unit/tolerance-aware comparison
Actual rendered WebUI Fans table/detail visual artifacts with API/UI/reference reconciliation for every channel
Preserved pre/post SEL/audit evidence, unchanged-control/no-stimulus proof and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: No mutation is intended. On ambiguity, stale/out-of-range reading, cooling fault or mismatch, stop and preserve/redact telemetry, UI and logs; obtain the authoritative map or limit. Do not clear logs, change fan control/thresholds, disconnect/reseat/stop a fan, inject a fault, add workload, reboot/reset, power-cycle or automatically retry.

source_conflict.reason: Title, procedure and Criteria consistently require all sixteen `_F` fan channels. The eight-entry/malformed DeepSeek query is an incomplete review-layer implementation, not a competing source requirement.

blocked.reason: Passive fan telemetry/status validation is standard and technically defined. `_F` semantics, physical mapping, population and contextual limits are finite Project execution inputs.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Authoritative `_F` semantics; sixteen-channel fan/rotor/controller map and population; actual modern/legacy resource shape; unit/range/threshold/freshness rules by operating context; WebUI mapping; trust and evidence policy.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; READ-ONLY FAN TELEMETRY REVIEW ONLY; NO REDFISH, WEBUI, LOG CLEAR, PWM, FAN, FAULT, WORKLOAD, RESET, POWER OR DUT ACTION EXECUTED

project_authority: The Project cooling design maps the sixteen vendor `_F` identifiers to physical fan/rotor/controller inputs and approves installed population plus operating-context-specific speed, unit, health and freshness limits. These finite inputs make the read-only comparison deterministic and fully automatable.
